chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn Amer, from Ahmad ibn Rizq, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala', from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A servant remained in the Fire for seventy autumns, and the autumn is seventy years. Then he asked Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, by the right of Muhammad and His Household, 'Have mercy on me.' So Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, revealed to Gabriel (peace be upon him): 'Descend to My servant and bring him out.' He said: 'O my Lord, how can I descend into the Fire?' He said: 'I have commanded it to be cool and safe for you.' He said: 'O my Lord, how do I know his location?' He said: 'He is in a pit from Sajin.' He descended into the Fire while being pulled by his face and brought him out. Then Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, said: 'O My servant, how long did you stay, calling upon Me in the Fire?' He said: 'I do not know, O my Lord.' He said: 'By My Majesty, had it not been for what you asked of Me, I would have prolonged your humiliation in the Fire. But I have decreed upon Myself that no servant asks Me by the right of Muhammad and His Household but I forgive him what was between Me and him. And I have forgiven you today.'

key_terms.بِحَقِّ مُحَمَّدٍ وَأَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: by the right of Muhammad and his Household
key_terms.جُبٍّ مِنْ سَجِين: a pit from Sajin (a place in Hell)
key_terms.مَا كَانَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ: what was between Me and him (sins/deeds)

ai.seo_question: How does invoking the right of Muhammad and his Household lead to forgiveness of sins in Hellfire?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the Shia doctrine of *Tawassul* (intercession) through the *Haqq* (right/authority) of the Ahl al-Bayt, demonstrating that even prolonged punishment in Hellfire can be reversed by this specific invocation. The narrative emphasizes God’s self-imposed decree (*Himma*) to forgive sins upon such requests, underscoring the mercy associated with the Prophet and his Household. It serves as a key textual basis for the belief that the intercession of the Imams holds independent efficacy in divine judgment.
